title: Community Sentencing and Other Rehabilitative Options
what_it_is: Community Sentencing and Other Rehabilitative Options

sections.label: Extending community-based sentencing regime
sections.summary: The speaker suggests considering extending community-based sentencing to offenders with more challenging mental disorders, given seven years of experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I am heartened by the approach we have taken thus far to deal with such offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, with the experience we have gained from the community-based sentencing regime over the past seven years, perhaps it is time we consider extending the community-based sentencing regime to offenders who suffer from more challenging mental disorders.

sections.label: Tan unsuitable for mandatory treatment order
sections.summary: Mr Tan was deemed not suitable for a mandatory treatment order because a huge multidisciplinary effort would be needed to turn around his condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Mr Tan was deemed not suitable for a mandatory treatment order (MTO), not because he is not at all treatable but because it will involve a huge multidisciplinary effort to effect a turnaround in his condition.

sections.label: Court sentenced Tan to jail
sections.summary: The Court decided he had to be punished and sentenced him to six months' jail for his offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the end, the Court decided he had to be punished.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He was sentenced to six months' jail for his offences.

sections.label: More powers for bespoke sentencing
sections.summary: The speaker suggests giving Courts more powers for bespoke sentencing arrangements across a wider spectrum of mental disorders, and monitoring offenders after release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Also, it would be in the public interest to monitor such offenders after they have been released and, where possible, for adjustments to be made to these offenders' circumstances and environment so as to lower the chances of them re-offending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I suggest that our Courts be given more powers to put in place bespoke sentencing arrangements drawing from a multitude of disciplines for a wider spectrum of mental disorders.

sections.label: UK Mental Health Act amendments
sections.summary: In the UK, 2008 amendments to the Mental Health Act abolished the treatability test in favour of the appropriate treatment test for sentencing offenders with mental disorders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What is also notable is that, in the UK, there were amendments made to the Mental Health Act in 2008 which abolished the "treatability test" in favour of the "appropriate treatment test" when considering sentencing orders for offenders with mental disorders.

sections.label: Structured framework for offender rehabilitation
sections.summary: The speaker says a structured community-focused legal framework and budget could support rehabilitation of offenders with mental disorders to reduce re-offending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Whilst I agree that there is no need for hard coding, it may be good to provide a structured community-focused legal framework and budget to support the rehabilitation of such offenders with mental disorders to reduce the likelihood of them re-offending and being charged in Court.

sections.label: Community-based rehabilitative programme framework
sections.summary: Stakeholder representatives helped a boy beyond their duties, and a legislative framework is suggested for a community-based rehabilitative programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this boy's case, the various stakeholder representatives went above their ordinary scope of duties to help him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I suggest that a legislative framework be provided to allow offenders to be put through this community-based rehabilitative programme.

sections.label: Review of minimum sentence offences
sections.summary: The regime limits community sentences or probation for adult offenders facing mandatory or specified minimum sentences, and a Parliamentary Question asked if MinLaw would review such offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The current regime circumscribes the Courts' power to impose community sentences or probation for adult offenders where the offence is one for which a mandatory or specified minimum sentence is prescribed by law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I filed a Parliamentary Question for oral answer asking if the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) would conduct a review of offences punishable by mandatory or specified minimum sentences to identify suitable offences for which community sentences or probation should be offered as sentencing options.

sections.label: Enlarging community-based sentencing review
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to enlarge its present review of community-based sentencing to include such offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For these reasons, I respectfully suggest that the Ministry enlarge the scope of its present review of the community-based sentencing to also include such offences.

sections.label: Reviewing community-based sentencing system
sections.summary: Seven years after community-based sentencing began, more experience has been gained, and a review is suggested to strengthen the system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Seven years on from the introduction of community-based sentencing, we have gained more experience in this area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I suggest that it is now time to review and take the necessary steps to strengthen the system based on the evolutionary approach advocated by the hon Minister.

sections.label: Strengthening rehabilitation signal
sections.summary: The Minister for Law introduced MTOs in 2010, and the impending CPC revision offers an opportunity to strengthen the signal of society's investment in offenders' well-being, treatment and rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2010, the Minister for Law made a laudable move in introducing MTOs under the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Seven years later, in light of the impending revision of the CPC, we now have an opportunity —

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: We now have an opportunity to strengthen the signal to these persons, their caregivers and families that, as a society, we remain invested in their well-being, treatment and rehabilitation.

sections.label: Expanding CBS scheme
sections.summary: One key plank of MinLaw's proposed CPC amendments is to expand the CBS scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In fact, one key plank of MinLaw's proposed amendments to the CPC is to expand the CBS scheme.

sections.label: Extending CBS to offences
sections.summary: The Government will relook legislation and consider extending Community-Based Sentencing to offences with specified minimum sentences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Justice would not be served by imposing CBS for such offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, we are prepared to explore whether eligibility for CBS can be extended to offences with specified minimum sentences, which are prescribed for relatively less serious offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Stakeholders we consulted had generally supported the continued exclusion of such offences, but we will relook the legislation and seriously consider whether CBS can be extended to these offences.

sections.label: Community support for mental health
sections.summary: The Government will address gaps in mental health support structures, but community support remains key to preventing re-offending.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To conclude, the Government will continue to identify and address any gaps in the support structures available for those with mental health conditions, but this cannot replace support from the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The key to prevent re-offending often lies in the person regularly receiving treatment, including taking his or her medication.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For this, there is no substitute for community support.
